# Stage 2R.5 and the Stage 2R decision gate

**Generated by `replay/stage2r_gate_report.py`. Do not hand-edit.**

A decision stage. Nothing was fitted, calibrated, ingested or repaired; no model default, assumption, threshold or output changed; D1, D2 and D3 are still in place exactly as V2 froze them. Stage 2R.0 through 2R.4 are complete through commit `0f98010`.

> # Gate verdict: NO DETECTABLE INCREMENTAL VALUE AT CURRENT RESOLUTION

> - No W2 calibration task is justified: W2.1 NOT JUSTIFIED; W2.2 NOT JUSTIFIED; W2.3 REQUIRED; W2.4 NOT JUSTIFIED; W2.5 NOT JUSTIFIED.
> - The replay detects no incremental value at effects larger than 5 net launch events, spread across at least two vintages, and the largest observed difference is 1 event.
> - The structural finding is a mismatch between the product's claim and its option set, not a defect whose repair would enable a meaningful calibration comparison. The resolution is to narrow the claim, which is a scope decision rather than a repair-and-reassess loop.

**This is not a finding that the model does not work, and it is not a proof of equivalence with a demand ranking.** Section 4 states the claim the evidence supports.

---

## 1. The product claim

Two products are hiding in the code, and only one of them is built.

| | claim | what it asserts |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | fixed-gauge route screening | given the configured gauge and an allowed schedule menu, is a candidate route economically supportable, and how do the supportable ones compare |
| **B** | fleet and frequency right-sizing | what aircraft and frequency should an airline use in this market |

### What the implementation supports

The WestJet study config lists **one gauge** (174 seats) and a schedule menu of **3x, 7x, 14x weekly**, with the comment that the project will not invent a regional-gauge transborder aircraft. Against that menu, 2R.3 measured:

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| decision rows | 463 |
| median load factor at 3x on the study gauge | **0.075** |
| feasibility floor | 0.50 |
| rows clearing the floor at 3x | 18 |
| rows with positive annual contribution at 3x | 9 |
| rows where no option clears the floor | **445** |
| rows selecting 3x | 461 |

**Claim B is not supported.** A selector whose menu contains one gauge and whose smallest schedule already exceeds the capacity the modelled demand can fill is not choosing an aircraft or a frequency. On 445 of 463 rows it never reaches a comparison, and the branch it takes instead returns the highest load factor, which is arithmetically the lowest frequency. 2R.1's control transition confirms the consequence: ranking by margin at the minimum option and at the chosen option are the same ordering, Spearman exactly 1.000 at every date.

**Claim A is supported, and most routes failing is a legitimate result under it.** A screen that says a thin transborder market cannot support a 737 at three weekly frequencies is answering the question it was asked. The defect is not the answer; it is the label on the component that produces it.

**Claim B is not rescued by expansion.** Supporting it would need smaller gauges the studied carriers do not fly on these routes, schedules below a real operation, and a fleet-assignment layer. All three are outside the roadmap's finish line, and the roadmap already declined to add carriers merely to raise N. Narrowing the claim is the cheaper and more honest move.

### Decision

> **The product is CLAIM A, fixed-gauge route screening.** **RETIRE / DE-SCOPE RIGHT-SIZING** as a validated model output.

### The terminology that should replace it

Not applied here. Recorded so the correction is mechanical when it is made.

| current wording | replacement |
|---|---|
| right-sizing, right-sized | fixed-gauge schedule evaluation |
| picks the frequency and gauge that maximize annual contribution | evaluates a fixed schedule menu on the study gauge and reports the best feasible option, or that none is feasible |
| best schedule | evaluated schedule |
| `chosen_freq_wk` in reader-facing text | evaluated frequency |
| optimization, optimizer | screening, evaluation |

The column name in the artifacts may stay `chosen_freq_wk`; what must change is every sentence that describes it as an optimisation result, and every place that reports a frequency without saying that the market had no feasible option.

## 2. Stage 2R.5: necessity gates

Every old Milestone B task, against all Stage 2R evidence. No task is carried forward because it appeared in the earlier plan.

| task | classification |
|---|---|
| **W2.1** DB1B Coupon and Ticket ingestion | **NOT JUSTIFIED** |
| **W2.2** marketing-brand mapping | **NOT JUSTIFIED** |
| **W2.3** one-stop reconstruction validation | **REQUIRED** |
| **W2.4** QSI fitting | **NOT JUSTIFIED** |
| **W2.5** fare segmentation | **NOT JUSTIFIED** |

### W2.1: DB1B Coupon and Ticket ingestion - NOT JUSTIFIED

- **mechanism it would improve**: itinerary and fare detail for the economics and competition layers
- **does that mechanism currently matter**: fare enters margin only through the break-even load factor, and 2R.3 shows the schedule decision is made by the feasibility floor before fare is consulted
- **could the replay validate the improvement**: no: 2R.0 bounds detectable improvement at five net launch events, which no fare refinement produces
- **cost**: high: two new DB1B tables, itinerary construction, a new mart
- **required for a defensible portfolio project**: no
- **recommendation**: do not run. The remaining claim does not need itinerary-level data.

### W2.2: marketing-brand mapping - NOT JUSTIFIED

- **mechanism it would improve**: resolve operating certificates to the brand a passenger buys, so the competitive set is not understated
- **does that mechanism currently matter**: already resolved where the studies consume it: unresolved regional flying is under 0.15% of hub-origin departures at all three hubs, and unresolved itineraries carry at most 3.5% of competitor preference
- **could the replay validate the improvement**: not applicable: the exposure is too small to move share
- **cost**: medium: effective-dating the brand map by vintage
- **required for a defensible portfolio project**: no
- **recommendation**: do not run. Record the residual as a documented limitation. The roadmap's D7 count is of the raw segment universe, not of what reaches a competitive set.

### W2.3: one-stop reconstruction validation - REQUIRED

- **mechanism it would improve**: the reconstructed one-stop competitive set, which carries 95% of competitor preference in the WestJet study
- **does that mechanism currently matter**: yes, decisively: share is one of only two layers that materially reorder, 85 of 88 WestJet candidates have no nonstop incumbent, and the existing share validation covers that structural regime with 2 markets
- **could the replay validate the improvement**: yes, and without new data: extend the existing `models/share_validation.py` check to the connection-only stratum
- **cost**: low: existing machinery, no new source
- **required for a defensible portfolio project**: yes, if the product keeps a competition or share layer
- **recommendation**: run the **validation**, not the original heuristic refit. Refitting detour bounds or connect time against MIDT or DB1B Coupon stays NOT JUSTIFIED.

### W2.4: QSI fitting - NOT JUSTIFIED

- **mechanism it would improve**: frequency and competitive responsiveness in the share model
- **does that mechanism currently matter**: no: 2R.3 shows the frequency exponent sets a crossover the candidate sets never approach, and 445 of 463 decisions never reach a frequency comparison at all
- **could the replay validate the improvement**: no: the same 2R.0 bound applies, and the fallback rows are unaffected by any exponent
- **cost**: high: calibration and holdout design
- **required for a defensible portfolio project**: no
- **recommendation**: do not run. The gate in the roadmap requires 2R.3 to identify frequency responsiveness as the bottleneck. It identifies the option set instead.

### W2.5: fare segmentation - NOT JUSTIFIED

- **mechanism it would improve**: fare structure in the economics layer
- **does that mechanism currently matter**: no: fare enters the ranking inside the same distance-driven factor as cost, and no fare-attributable distortion was found in 2R.1 or 2R.3
- **could the replay validate the improvement**: no
- **cost**: medium to high
- **required for a defensible portfolio project**: no
- **recommendation**: do not run.

### Evidence for W2.2 and W2.3

These two share a layer, and the measurements separate them cleanly.

**What the competitive set is made of.** Preference is the same QSI-lite quantity `comp_pref_sum` is built from.

| study | itineraries | nonstop | one-stop | one-stop share of competitor preference | itineraries on an unresolved certificate | their share of preference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| westjet_yyc | 272 | 3 | 269 | **95.2%** | 4 | 2.9% |
| alaska_sea | 370 | 1 | 369 | **98.4%** | 0 | 0.0% |
| porter_yyz | 544 | 43 | 501 | **75.0%** | 7 | 3.5% |

**Brand resolution where the studies consume it.**

| study | hub | hub-origin departures | flown by a regional operator | unresolved | unresolved share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| westjet_yyc | YYC | 14,665 | 1,543 | 3 | **0.02%** |
| alaska_sea | SEA | 206,069 | 56,238 | 177 | **0.09%** |
| porter_yyz | YYZ | 60,097 | 34,140 | 83 | **0.14%** |

W2.2 is settled by that table. The brand map already resolves more than 99.8% of hub-origin flying at all three hubs, and the itineraries that do carry an unresolved certificate contribute at most 3.5% of competitor preference. The roadmap's D7 figure counts unmapped triples in the raw segment universe, which is a different and much larger population than the flying a candidate's competitive set actually consumes.

**Where the share model has and has not been checked.** `models/share_validation.py` scores incumbents with the same QSI-lite the proposals use and compares against observed DB1B ticketing shares.

| nonstop carriers in the market | markets | rows | MAE, share points | passenger-weighted MAE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2 | 17 | 3.7 | 5.6 |
| 1 | 26 | 173 | 6.9 | 18.9 |
| 2 | 17 | 132 | 5.7 | 13.3 |
| 3 | 12 | 99 | 5.2 | 11.0 |
| 4 | 4 | 36 | 4.3 | 6.9 |
| 5 | 5 | 46 | 4.4 | 9.0 |

**This is why W2.3 is the one required task.** The check covers 66 markets, of which 2 have no nonstop carrier. The WestJet study lives almost entirely in that stratum: 85 of 88 candidates have no nonstop incumbent, and one-stop reconstruction carries 95% of competitor preference. The layer that does most of the differentiating is validated in a regime the flagship study barely occupies. Closing that needs no new source: it is a stratum extension of a check that already exists.

## 3. Final treatment of D1, D2, D3A and D3B

None is implemented here.

| defect | decision |
|---|---|
| **D1** corridor growth vintage | **MUST FIX BEFORE FINAL AUDIT** |
| **D2** right-sizing | **RETIRE / DE-SCOPE RIGHT-SIZING** |
| **D3A** survey-ceiling compression | **DOCUMENTATION / LIMITATION** |
| **D3B** fixed 4,000 publication floor | **ACCEPTABLE DOCUMENTED APPROXIMATION** |

### D1: corridor growth vintage - MUST FIX BEFORE FINAL AUDIT

**Why.** a demand level wrong by a factor of 5.4 at the 2023-01 cutoff is a correctness error regardless of what it does to a metric, and 2R.4 measured exactly what it moves

**Required before or after.** before and after on: median demand and margin by study and date; the demand-only and margin rankings, which 2R.4 predicts are unchanged for WestJet; WestJet verdict counts, predicted unchanged; Porter verdicts, predicted to move; Family 1 and Family 4, predicted unchanged. Any departure from those predictions is a finding in itself.

### D2: right-sizing - RETIRE / DE-SCOPE RIGHT-SIZING

**Why.** 445 of 463 decisions never reach a comparison, and the infeasibility fallback is arithmetically identical to returning the minimum frequency. Repairing it means adding gauges the studied carriers do not fly and schedules below a real operation, which is a different model

**Required before or after.** no model change. The remaining logic is honest as **fixed-gauge schedule feasibility**: the engine evaluates a small predefined schedule menu on the study gauge and reports whether any option is feasible and what it earns. `chosen_freq_wk` becomes `evaluated_freq_wk` in reader-facing text and stops being described as an optimisation result.

### D3A: survey-ceiling compression - DOCUMENTATION / LIMITATION

**Why.** the tied block sits entirely below demand rank 50, reaches no demand top 20 and contains no WestJet launch, so it costs the baseline nothing. Its only cost is the downstream promotion of ceiling rows into the margin top k, and the ranking decision in section 5 removes the surface on which that would mislead

**Required before or after.** document in LIMITATIONS as a censoring assumption with its measured tail position. No code change.

### D3B: fixed 4,000 publication floor - ACCEPTABLE DOCUMENTED APPROXIMATION

**Why.** it is a real level error, but 2R.2 shows correcting it unties nothing and at 2024-01 would capture one more row, not fewer. It moves the capped block relative to anchored markets in the tail, which is below every scored top k. The cost is per-vintage floor recovery from StatCan for a change with no measured effect on any reader-facing output

**Required before or after.** document the fixed floor and the true 280 to 3,090 range in LIMITATIONS, next to D3A and explicitly separate from it. Revisit only if a future study scores a top k that the capped block reaches.

**D3A and D3B stay separate.** D3A is compression, which is inherent to censoring and survives any floor value. D3B is level, which a floor correction fixes and which unties nothing. 2R.2 measured both: the tie block is the same size at every floor from 280 to 4,000 and grows as the floor falls.

## 4. The predictive claim

The strongest wording the evidence supports, and the wording that should appear in every reader-facing document:

> On the WestJet Calgary historical replay, the full engine showed **no detectable incremental ranking value over a demand-only baseline at effects larger than the study's resolution**. Smaller effects remain unresolved. This is a bounded negative result, not a demonstration that the engine is equivalent to ranking by modelled demand.

It must be published with its bound attached, from Stage 2R.0:

| bound | value |
|---|---|
| distinct launch events in the flagship study | **10** (on 15 positive rows; a launch inside two cutoff windows is a positive at both) |
| decision vintages | **3** |
| optimistic detectability floor | **about 5 net launch events, spread across at least two vintages** |
| largest observed difference | 1 launch event |
| effects confined to one vintage | not detectable at any magnitude the sample permits (0 of the single-date allocations tested exclude zero) |
| k=20 | no improvement is expressible at all, so the zero difference there is saturation |

The floor is called optimistic deliberately: 2R.0 derives it from an oracle construction scored against an interval that omits decision-vintage uncertainty. Both push it down.

### Is that enough for the portfolio?

**Yes, and it is the stronger story.** The project's stated premise is validation and falsification, not predictive superiority. What it can now show is a point-in-time replay built before the results were seen, a pre-registered protocol, a measured resolution limit, a mechanical explanation for the null, four structural defects found by the project's own instruments, and a scope narrowed to what the evidence supports. A claim of predictive superiority resting on 10 launch events across 3 vintages would be the weaker artifact, and an interviewer who checked would find it.

2R.1 adds the part a bare null cannot: **why**. Away from capacity `margin_pct` is a monotone function of captured demand times a distance-driven fare-over-cost factor, so the engine is a demand ranking tilted by share and distance rather than an independent signal. The null is explained, not merely reported.

## 5. Is the margin ranking a valid public output?

What a continuous public ranking would be ordering:

| study | date | candidates | clearing the feasibility floor | with positive margin | not PASS | best margin in the top ten | worst |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| alaska_sea | 202201 | 45 | 1 | 0 | 0 | -97% | -214% |
| alaska_sea | 202301 | 43 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -470% | -709% |
| alaska_sea | 202401 | 43 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -206% | -355% |
| porter_yyz | 202401 | 88 | 9 | 2 | 2 | 18% | -57% |
| westjet_yyc | 202201 | 88 | 8 | 7 | 7 | 51% | -23% |
| westjet_yyc | 202301 | 80 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -1,134% | -3,191% |
| westjet_yyc | 202401 | 76 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -253% | -618% |

At 5 of 7 study-dates the published top ten would be an ordering of markets whose **best** case is a negative margin, in three cases beyond a hundred percent negative. Ordering them implies a precision and an actionability the underlying numbers do not carry, and 2R.2 shows the same ranking pulls uninformative survey-ceiling rows into its top k where the demand ranking never does.

A feasibility gate removes that second problem completely: **0 of 172 survey-ceiling rows clear the floor** at any frequency, the highest reaching a load factor of 0.078. Under option B the tied block cannot appear in an ordered set at all, which is what makes D3A a documentation item rather than a fix.

### Decision

> **Option B: verdict first, ordering only within candidates that clear the feasibility floor.** Everything below the floor is presented as an unordered PASS set with the reason it failed, not as ranks 11 through 88.

Option C is too strong: where a market does clear the floor the ordering is meaningful, and Porter has such markets. Option A is indefensible for the reason above.

**The continuous ranking is retained as a research instrument.** Family 4 needs a total order over identical rows to compare against the demand percentile, and that comparison is the project's central result. What changes is its status: it is a comparator inside the replay, never a recommendation ordering in the product. No implementation change is made here.

## 6. Minimal remaining work plan

Only work required to reach portfolio ready. Nothing is carried forward from the old roadmap without evidence in this document.

| # | kind | task | why it is required | how it is verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | correctness | Fix D1 in isolation under a change report | the corridor growth term is a raw two-year T-100 ratio with no COVID handling; demand at 2023-01 is wrong by 5.4x | 2R.4's before-and-after table, including the predictions it makes: WestJet rankings and verdicts unchanged, Porter verdicts move |
| T2 | scope | Retire the right-sizing claim across the reader-facing surfaces | 15 lines in 7 files describe an optimisation the model does not perform | the audit table in section 1 must come back empty, and the consistency tests must cover the replacement wording |
| T3 | validation | Extend the share validation to the connection-only stratum (W2.3) | the layer that does most of the differentiating is checked in a regime the flagship study barely occupies | MAE by market structure with a usable n in the zero-nonstop stratum, published in docs/validation.md |
| T4 | documentation | Document D3A, D3B and the resolution bound in LIMITATIONS | three findings currently live only in Stage 2R documents | the consistency tests, which already guard reader-facing numbers |
| T5 | verification | Re-run the frozen replay and the V2 comparison after T1 | V2 is the scoreboard and D1 is the only model change | a new freeze document stating what moved and why, per V2 section 6 |
| T6 | audit | Final audit and packaging | the project's own definition of done | `make all && make test` green from clean, `make reproducibility`, consistency tests, PROGRESS.md current |

**Explicitly not in the plan.** W2.1, W2.2, W2.4 and W2.5; any new carrier or study; ADS-B; new APIs or frontends; smaller gauges or sub-3x schedules; any further tuning of a metric. The D3B floor correction is out by the decision in section 3, and D3A needs no code.

### Order and dependencies

T1 before T5. T2, T3 and T4 are independent of both and of each other. T6 last. Only T1 changes model behaviour; T3 adds a validation output and changes no model default.

## 7. Finish line

**6 material tasks remain**, of which **one** changes the model (T1), one adds a validation (T3), two are documentation and scope corrections (T2, T4), and two are verification (T5, T6).

For comparison, the superseded plan carried five W2 ingestion and calibration programmes, four of which this document classifies NOT JUSTIFIED and the fifth of which is replaced by a validation that needs no new data.

No new scope was created by this stage.

## What was and was not done

- No repair. D1, D2, D3A and D3B are exactly as V2 froze them.
- No model behaviour, assumption, threshold or scoring function changed. `SURVEY_THRESHOLD` unchanged.
- No data ingested, no `make data`, no network call.
- No W2 task started.
- V2 not modified. No reader-facing document rewritten: the terminology correction is specified here and left for T2.
